methodology: Use AutoModelForSequenceClassification on an MNLI checkpoint as the inference entry point, represent each pair as two directed premise-hypothesis encodings (sentence1->sentence2 and sentence2->sentence1), and score paraphrase by the averaged entailment-minus-contradiction logit margin, differing from the zero-shot pipeline by operating directly in NLI label space and from all cosine or prompted methods by using a symmetric discriminative recast.
plan: 1) In one code cell install transformers, datasets, scikit-learn, and tqdm; 2) import torch, numpy, load_dataset, AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification, accuracy_score, f1_score, classification_report, and tqdm; 3) set device to MPS when available and print it; 4) choose model_name = 'typeform/distilbert-base-uncased-mnli', load tokenizer and model, move model to device, set eval mode, and inspect label ids to find entailment and contradiction indices; 5) load glue/mrpc validation and extract sentence1, sentence2, and y_true; 6) in batches tokenize both directions, first (sentence1, sentence2) and then (sentence2, sentence1), with padding and truncation; 7) for each direction run the model under torch.no_grad(), extract logits, compute margin = logits[:, entailment_id] - logits[:, contradiction_id], and average the two directional margins; 8) predict paraphrase when the averaged margin is greater than 0, producing y_pred; 9) compute accuracy, F1, and classification_report; 10) print several examples with both directional margins and the first 10 mistakes; 11) build and display a summary dict with dataset, split, model, device, num_examples, accuracy, and f1.
